correctness.rationale: For d≥2, ℓ>0, 0<a<ℓ the precise Euclidean body is |x_i|≤ℓ/2, |x_i−x_j|≤ℓ−a. Every nonempty W⊆[d] contributes an extreme vertex with coordinates ℓ/2 on W and a−ℓ/2 outside, plus its antipode, as confirmed from the original 2020 vertex classification and 2024 centered inequalities. Squared norms depend only on k=|W|, and consecutive differences equal a(ℓ−a)>0; hence d shells and 2 binomial multiplicities, with only ±ℓ/2 * 1 at outermost radius ℓ√d/2. Opposite poles give the sharp and unique Euclidean minimal enclosing sphere. Every center z of an inscribed Euclidean ball of radius ρ satisfies |z_i|+ρ≤ℓ/2, |z_i−z_j|+√2ρ≤ℓ−a. These constraints are necessary and sufficient for all facets. At z=0 the minimum clearance gives exact radius; at the coordinate-controlled regime all z_i=0, while in difference-controlled regime all z_i are equal and coordinate facets bound a diagonal segment. This proves the sharp transition including equality case. Independently enumerated exact rational vertex-shell counts in d=2..6 and checked symbolic formulas; source checker inspects d≤8. The proof, not the finite enumerations, covers all d.
residual_risks: Realization is fixed by Euclidean coordinates; affine equivalence to other cubic polytopes does not preserve radii.
Strict a range needed for d distinct shells; degenerate endpoints explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: The 2020 full primary text supplies the complete labeled vertex combinatorics, and 2024 full primary text gives the halfspace/zonotope description and volumes. A later published related Resultary finding DOES explicitly give the unique Euclidean minimum enclosing sphere and its pole contacts, so that particular subclaim is already covered and not new. However it treats John and Löwner ellipsoids, not the complete Euclidean incenter phase diagram or d strict vertex shell multiplicities. The surviving complete Euclidean inball center classification is neither a volume identity nor an ellipsoid contact theorem.
residual_risks: Do not claim priority for the circumradius/poles; those already occur explicitly in the ellipsoid paper.
A 2025 paper on incidence numbers/symmetries of isocanted cubes was not inspected in full; possible equivalent Chebyshev-center discussion remains a narrower literature risk.

value.rationale: The complete incenter locus and its sharp one-point-to-segment phase transition are intrinsic Euclidean geometric data of a natural all-dimensional class of zonotopes. They explain when metric optimality loses uniqueness; exact strict vertex shell multiplicities also record radial stratification useful for studying contact and non-isotropic approximations. The outer sphere subclaim is known, but does not remove mathematical value of the distinct complete center classification.
residual_risks: The radius itself is a short consequence of halfspace distance, but the complete all-parameter optimizing-center geometry is the distinctive motivation.

final_claim: The d-dimensional centered isocanted cube has d strict vertex norm shells with squared radii kℓ²/4+(d-k)(ℓ/2-a)² and multiplicities 2*binom(d,k); its Euclidean inradius is min(ℓ/2,(ℓ-a)/√2), and the full incenter set changes from {0} to a diagonal segment at a*=ℓ(1−1/√2).
limitations: The minimum enclosing sphere/pole portion is previously covered by a separate published ellipsoid study and is not counted as an original subresult.
Endpoint a=0 shell coalescence and a=ℓ dimension collapse are excluded; metrics depend on centered cubic realization.
